newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Volkswagen on target for 96 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Volkswagen on target for 96 profit.

text.p: Europe's largest carmaker, Volkswagen AG (VW), on Wednesday reported a 56 percent leap in
pre-tax profit over the first nine months of the year and said it was heading for higher full year earnings and sales.

Volkswagen said in a statement that pre-tax profit rose to 1.48 billion marks ($970.6 million), between January and September, up from 948 million a year ago. Group sales climbed 14.2 percent to a record 74.49 billion marks.
"We expect better profit and sales than the year before," a company spokesman said.
After-tax profit climbed to 465 million marks from 185 million for the same period in 1995.
"The Volkswagen figures are good figures, especially when you consider the gathering difficulties of other companies in the sector."John Lawson, car analyst at Salomon Brothers in London, said.
Michael Schickling, an analyst at Schroeder Munchmeyer Hengst in Frankfurt, said the figures were better than expected.
"The third quarter operating profit figure was particularly good and it looks as if VW will reach its operating profit target figure in the current business year."
Schickling said he thought the group would see an increase in sales of 10 percent in the current year, although sales in France had fallen somewhat.
Some analysts tend to view VW profit figures with scepticism because of the accounting and tax provisions the company often makes.
The carmaker was one of the only only winners in afternoon trade on the IBIS DAX index, which gauges electronic trade in the 30 leading German shares.
At one point, the overall IBIS DAX index was down 1.37 percent, while VW shares were up 0.78 percent.
The carmaker has surpassed its own expectations for much of this year, winning European market share by fighting to keep costs and prices down, analysts said.

"This confirms VW as one of the winners in the sector. VW has shown excellent growth rates in terms of sales -- the deutschemark growth rate helped -- and it is one of the fastest growing car companies in the current situation," Lawson said.
Volkswagen said car production rose 8.7 percent during the first nine months to 2,741,914 units, while worldwide deliveries to customers climbed 12.6 percent to 2,986,977 units.
"The income figure is only a partial indicator of earnings potential, but the quarter-on-quarter growth in earnings is quite impressive -- 73 percent on the third quarter of 1995," said Lawson.
VW's share price deserved "a round of applause", he said.
